I will keep it simple and stay with the wheat-maize rotation on the same land. In Quzhou County, that is the system I trust most because it fits the climate, the local water conditions, and the way I already know how to farm. I would not spread myself across too many crops, because at my age I would rather manage a familiar system well than chase a crop with higher risk or more labor. I will put my land into winter wheat first and then summer maize after wheat harvest. For seed, I will use improved or hybrid seed where it helps yield and standability, but I will still choose varieties that are common locally and easy to manage. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage for wheat planting because it is practical and common, and then mostly no-tillage or very light disturbance for summer maize after wheat so I can save time and hold moisture. I will use moderate fertilizer, not excessive, because too much input costs money and does not always bring enough extra grain. I will irrigate wheat more than maize because wheat in this area usually depends more on timely watering, especially around jointing and grain filling. I will spray only as needed, mainly for weeds and common diseases or insects, because I want to control losses but keep costs under control. My goal is stable yield, manageable labor, and dependable cash flow from grain I know I can produce.
